subject: Rapid SLO decisioning: hosted vs dedicated capacity (post-call follow-up)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@lumenpay.com>; LumenPay Platform Team <ops@lumenpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Rapid SLO decisioning: hosted vs dedicated capacity (post-call follow-up)

Hi Priya / LumenPay team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of requirements we captured
- Peak online QPS observed during checkout: ~12k requests/minute (bursty, 2–3x peaks during promos)
- Typical generation workload: 1–4 prompts per request, average output ~120 tokens; p95 latency target for end-to-end response <= 120ms when running in production
- Data residency: user PII must stay in us-west; initial scope is no on-prem requirement, but you flagged potential VPC requirement later if we go to production multi-region
- Budget note: strong sensitivity to per-token cost — finance will expect an A/B cost comparison before committing to a reserved pool

Our suggested path based on the call
1) Short pilot (2 weeks) to validate both latency and steady-state unit cost. Objectives: prove p95 latency < 120ms under your representative workload, measure per-token cost with prefix caching enabled.
2) Start pilot using Hosted API with a temporary Dedicated pool reserved for peak windows (we can enable burst capacity). This lets you avoid an immediate private deployment while still getting predictable throughput for peak hours.
3) If the pilot shows consistent p95 > 120ms or stateful requirements force placement, we will evaluate Private (VPC) as a follow-up phase.

Asks / action items for LumenPay
- Please share the canonical traffic sample (one week) and a small set of representative prompts (8–12) we can use for benching — you mentioned you could export June data.
- Confirm whether the 120ms p95 is for the full-stack (app + network) or just Redwood inference time — we assumed Redwood inference time is budgeted to ~70–90ms and app/network makes up the remainder.

Proposed timeline
- Bench plan + pilot scope doc (we will send) by EOD Friday (I'll attach the pilot-scope).
- Pilot kickoff: target week of Jul 20 — 2-week run with daily sampling dashboards.

Attaching a short scope doc (pilot-scope-summary.pdf) and will follow up with a bench plan.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt

Subject: Re: Rapid SLO decisioning: hosted vs dedicated capacity (post-call follow-up)

Thanks Hannah — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Traffic sample: attaching the June export (lumenpay-traffic-profile-june.csv). It's in 1-min granularity; you can see the promo day spike on June 18. The pattern is bursty; we expect a similar shape for upcoming campaigns.

2) Latency target: the 120ms p95 is our customer-visible Android app SLO (end-to-end). We estimate the app + network adds 30–50ms, so Redwood inference should aim for ~70–90ms p95 as you suggested.

3) Data residency: for the pilot, us-west is sufficient. We will need VPC/on-prem discussions only if we move to a production arrangement with sensitive customer segments.

4) Budget: procurement wants a headroom cost estimate for both a Hosted-first pilot and a Dedicated reserved quote (monthly) so they can compare.

We are available for kickoff Jul 20 — please send pilot runbook and a short quote for the dedicated option ahead of kickoff.

Attaching: lumenpay-traffic-profile-june.csv

Best,
Priya

Subject: Re: Rapid SLO decisioning: hosted vs dedicated capacity (post-call follow-up)

Hi Priya / team — thanks for the traffic file, that helps. Quick technical read and our recommendation for the pilot: 

Preliminary analysis (from the sample)
- Baseline QPS distribution shows 10–15 minute spikes that are ~2.5x baseline; sustained high during promos.
- Average prompt length and output confirm the 120-token expectation; payload sizes are moderate.

Pilot recommendation (optimize for risk reduction)
- Start with Hosted API for control-plane simplicity, but provision a temporary Dedicated pool for the expected promo windows in the pilot. Why: this validates network and model performance under realistic load without long-term commitment.
- Technical knobs during pilot: continuous batching tuned to 20–30ms target batch interval, prefix/KV caching enabled for repeated prompts, and model quantization to int8 where functionally acceptable.
- Bench plan: we will run distributed load tests that simulate client-level parallelism (connection churn, retries) to ensure p95 inference time stays in 70–90ms.

Deliverables I will provide by Friday
- redwood-pilot-benchmark-plan.md (bench steps, k6 scripts, metrics to capture)
- preliminary cost delta estimate: Hosted baseline vs Dedicated reserved (monthly run-rate) for an expected production-of-record workload (ballpark numbers so procurement can plan)

Questions for your ops team
- Can you provide a short list of 8–12 representative prompts (exact strings) and a stable API key or test token we can use for synthetic testing?
- Any network egress filters or proxies we should know about for connecting to us-west endpoints?

If this sounds good we will compile the bench plan + quote and book the kickoff for Jul 20.

Thanks — Ben

Great — thank you both. Pilot plan and the bench scripts sound like the right approach. A couple of final asks before kickoff: 

- Please send the dedicated-capacity quote (monthly) and an estimated per-token cost during the pilot (hosted vs dedicated) so procurement has numbers to review.
- We will provide the 8–12 prompts and a test token by EOD Monday.
- Confirm whether the temporary dedicated pool can be scoped to only the promo windows (scheduled hours) to reduce cost during the pilot.

We are OK to proceed with Jul 20 kickoff pending the quote. Please loop in your billing contact when you send the quote.

Thanks — Priya
